transcript_segments.text: there's a man outside the shop with three coins two carrier bags and a cigarette
he keeps forgetting to smoke someone asks him for change
he laughs not because it's funny because the till inside his chest already
says no then he gives them one of the coins
some people call that poor judgement i call it theology
minimum wage messiah with holes in his trainers turning water into tap water and still sharing
later he's got rent in the rears bread reduced
after eight a phone with one percent and a cracked little
faith but he'll split a sandwich like a sacred
transaction half for his hunger half for compassion
no press no plaque no grateful committee just kindness with a receipt too thin
to claim back from the city meanwhile a man with seven spare houses
says tax is a burden from one of his couches says wealth needs freedom says markets need
air says people should try being born with a chair
and somewhere in town a cleaner counts pennies to buy someone tea
who is fewer than any tell me again who the economy blesses
tell me again who keeps failing the test minimum wage messiah empty pockets open
hands giving away nothing like his loaves upon
the sand those with everything keep asking what it
costs while the ones with almost nothing pay the
debt for all we've lost if mercy had to pay slip they'd be rich
beyond belief but the kindest little prophets still can't
afford relief i've seen saints in supermarket uniforms
name tags crooked souls outworn mothers at tills with feet full of thunder
scanning cheap pasta and swallowing hunger they round down prices when nobody sees
slip extra napkins beside weak coffees they say don't worry love like it is inexpensive
to sound that gentle while life gets offensive and the rich the rich have opinions about
other people's fridges they say work harder they say spend less
from a lunch that could cover three months of stress
they call tax theft with the straight little face
like survival is greedy and hoarding is grace they got offshore islands for feelings and
funds little sunny accounts where accountability
runs but ask them to pay so a kid can eat dinner
suddenly the mansion gets spiritually thinner
minimum wage messiah empty pockets open hands
giving away nothing like his loaves upon the sand
those with everything keep asking what it costs
while the ones with almost nothing pay the debt for all we've lost
if mercy had a pay slip they'd be rich beyond belief
but the kindest little prophets still can't afford relief
and i know poverty isn't holy let's not dress pain up and call it a lesson
nobody should have to become generous because the system left them nothing else
to give there is no romance in an empty meter
no moral wisdom in choosing between heating and dinner
but there is something almost impossible about a person counting their last coins
then looking at another person and thinking you first
that should shame every golden tower in the skyline
that should rattle every locked drawer where the surplus sleeps
that should make the comfortable feel audited maybe holiness isn't thunder
maybe it's bus fare handed over by someone walking home
maybe it's a coat on a cold a back of tea paid forward
a tired nurse smuggling a joke through a 12 hour shift
maybe grace is the minimum payment made by people or bread with drowning in interest
maybe love is the only currency that gets bigger when spent
maybe one day we start praising the poor for surviving the wound
and start billing the people who sold us the knife
until then there's a man by the shop with two coins now
one carrier bag and no cigarettes still laughing still broke still richer
than the men who could save the world and asked her for a deduction
minimum wage messiah empty pockets open hands
giving away nothing like its lows upon the sand those with everything keep asking what it cost
while the ones with almost nothing pay the debt for all we've lost
if mercy had a pay slip they'd be rich beyond belief
but the kindest little prophets still can't afford belief
minimum wage messiah walking home beneath the rain
gave away his nothing and called it someone's gain
the till says no the heart says try anyway
somewhere a billionaire is explaining fairness to a chandelier
somewhere else a hungry man breaks bread
and the whole broken world almost balances
almost balances
